solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perhaps deconstruct music for Rattle?

definitions.meaning: taking a composition apart, undoing the act of composing, read as DIS- plus COMPOSE
to rattle someone is to unsettle or fluster them

explanation.surface: A question about the conductor Sir Simon Rattle, as if he might take music to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Rattle looks like the conductor's name, but it is the verb meaning to fluster.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unsettle their composure, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Broken seat

definitions.meaning: slang for the backside, what one sits on

explanation.surface: A chair with a broken seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses this word both for something not working and for the buttocks.

clue.text: Bellow was one constant emitted by upcoming American director

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top
emitted by means the constant is sent out of the director's name

parts.note: George Lucas is the American director of Star Wars
C is the constant for the speed of light

explanation.surface: Someone bellowed a constant stream of noise from an American director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emitted by' removes C from LUCAS, giving LUAS, which 'upcoming' reverses. Bellow is the novelist Saul Bellow, not a shout.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel-winning novelist Bellow had this first name, so he was one example.

clue.text: No left-winger directly flanks one of opposed parties

parts.note: the flanks of something are its outside
the right and the left are opposed political sides

explanation.surface: A political note that no left-winger sides with one of the opposed parties.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an old football position: a forward playing wide on the right, so certainly not on the left wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger on the right of the pitch is by position never a left-winger, and politically right too.

clue.text: Parking in good time to reach such gates, one'll be late

parts.note: arriving in good time means arriving early

explanation.surface: Advice on parking in good time to get to the gates, or you will be late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead: the departed are said to reach heaven's gates of pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven's gates are traditionally described as made of pearl, reached once a person has died.

clue.text: Flag stone also placed on a road

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
and means also

explanation.surface: A flagstone also laid on a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag stone' suggests paving, but Flag is the definition and stone gives ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner or flag carried as an emblem.

clue.text: Frivolity daughter's to pay for

parts.note: frivolity is light-hearted fun

explanation.surface: A parent grumbling that their daughter's frivolous pleasures are what they must pay for.
explanation.definitionFit: To fund something is to provide the money for it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Lion shot with airgun that's second-hand

indicators.note: shot as in wrecked or broken means the combined letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lion shot with an air rifle that was bought second-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unoriginal is derivative, borrowed from others' ideas, as second-hand ideas are.

clue.text: Habit involving snow I mixed for narcotic effect

indicators.note: involving means the garment wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a habit is a garment such as a nun's dress

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of snow and I are jumbled

explanation.surface: A habit containing mixed snow, cocaine slang, has a narcotic effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snow' tempts as cocaine slang, fitting the narcotic surface, but it is only letters for 'mixed' to shuffle with I.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic induces sleepiness, so heavy-eyed sleepiness is its effect.

clue.text: Possibly healthy dessert craze includes odd rituals

indicators.note: includes means the craze word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a craze is a passing fad

indicators.note: odd signals that the letters of rituals are in a strange, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A dieting fad that involves strange rituals, presented as possibly good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like it describes the rituals but signals that their letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of mixed chopped fruit is a dessert that can claim to be healthy, hence the 'possibly'.

clue.text: Country for departure?

definitions.meaning: food bought '...' is taken away, so it is for leaving with

explanation.surface: A traveller asking which country to head for when leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a West African republic; split as two words it means for taking away.

clue.text: Bonding couple excited re erotic plan

indicators.note: excited means the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A romantic couple aroused by a racy scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonding couple' suggests lovers, but it is chemistry: two shared particles form a covalent bond.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, two shared particles form a covalent bond between atoms, so they are a couple that bonds.

clue.text: Woman politely sent back whoppers after herb trifles

indicators.note: after says the rest of the pieces follow the herb

parts.note: dill is a feathery culinary herb

indicators.note: sent back means the polite word for a woman is read backwards

parts.note: lady is the polite term for a woman
whoppers are big lies

explanation.surface: A woman returns tall stories after being given a herb, a muddled domestic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns LADY into YDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle is to waste time idly, which is the same as dawdling, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Distant traveller getting brilliant clip uploaded in time

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the time word

parts.note: a span is a period of time
ace means brilliant

indicators.note: uploaded in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to mow is to clip grass

explanation.surface: Someone far away gets a great video clip uploaded in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uploaded' turns MOW into WOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A female astronaut journeys far beyond Earth, a distant traveller.

clue.text: Concerned over America, therefore allowed to go first

indicators.note: to go first says the therefore and allowed words come before the rest

parts.note: so means therefore
licit means lawful or allowed
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
US is America

explanation.surface: Someone worried about America, so permitted to go ahead first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is not a positional indicator here but O, the cricket abbreviation; 'to go first' puts SO and LICIT ahead of O and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Being solicitous means anxious and attentive, showing concern for someone.

clue.text: Conventional thing often tied in proportional representation

indicators.note: in places the tied thing within the abbreviation

parts.note: a rope is something frequently tied in knots

explanation.surface: A political observation that some convention is usually bound up with proportional representation.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper behaviour is correct and conventional, a synonym.

clue.text: Proportional representation voided for lawsuit

indicators.note: voided means emptied, so the word for loses its middle

parts.note: an action is a legal suit

explanation.surface: A proportional voting system being thrown out in favour of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: After 15-across used PR as the voting system, here the phrase is the definition: a number such as three-quarters represents a proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A numerical part of a whole expresses a proportion, so it is one way of representing it.

clue.text: Principally, Nemo's aboard, using this in leagues under sea

definitions.text: Principally, Nemo's aboard, using this in leagues under sea

indicators.note: principally signals taking the principal, leading letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Captain Nemo is aboard his submarine on the voyage of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: Jules Verne's Captain Nemo commands this vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemo's submarine in Verne's novel bears this name, used for travel leagues beneath the sea.

clue.text: Chinchilla, not hot at all, surprisingly cold?

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the remaining letters come out in an unexpected order
H is hot on taps, and at all means every one goes, so both are removed from chinchilla

explanation.surface: A furry chinchilla that is not warm in the least, oddly enough, is cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hot at all' strips both Hs from CHINCHILLA, leaving CINCILLA, which 'surprisingly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinical as in detached and unemotional describes a cold manner.

clue.text: Attempts retreat into road in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means the combined letters are read from the end back
into puts the retreat word inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a road
a lair is an animal's hideaway or retreat

explanation.surface: Attempts to retreat into a road while reversing a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' acts on the whole combination after the insertion, not just the retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Trials are tests or attempts at something, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Preserve state benefit, scrapping nothing that's useful if power's cut

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it

indicators.note: scrapping means throwing the zero out of the benefit word

parts.note: the dole is British state unemployment benefit
O is nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A warning about preserving state benefits while scrapping anything of use when power is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapping' removes O from DOLE, leaving DLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax light with a wick gives light in a power cut, so it is useful then.

clue.text: Crew that rows craft backwards in victories uses gym machines

indicators.note: in places the crew and craft inside the victories

parts.note: victories are wins
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

indicators.note: backwards means the word for craft is reversed

parts.note: craft as skill is art

explanation.surface: A winning rowing crew that also trains on gym machines.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing boat's crew of eight oarsmen; 'backwards' reverses only the craft word.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise using weighted equipment at a gym is a hyphenated verb for strength workouts.

clue.text: Call for attention, meeting private master of posturing?

parts.note: yo is a shout to get attention
a GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A shout for attention as one meets a private soldier who is a master of posing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posturing' suggests showing off, but means yoga postures.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher of yoga is adept at holding bodily postures, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Some weighty matters must overturn a delusion

indicators.note: must overturn in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Some weighty issues must overturn a mistaken belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A false belief widely held is a fiction, so it can be called a delusion.

clue.text: Anchor fell

definitions.meaning: to anchor a boat is to secure or tie it up
a fell is a high stretch of open hill land in northern England

explanation.surface: A ship's anchor that dropped, or fell, overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but here is a noun for upland country.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor is to secure a vessel; moorland is open upland, as a fell is.

clue.text: Youth I hate inwardly enters covered in blood of ancient fighters

indicators.note: enters puts the youth and the rest inside the bloody word

parts.note: gory means bloodstained
a lad is a youth

indicators.note: inwardly takes only the inner letters of hate

explanation.surface: A young man confesses inner hatred as he enters, bloodied, like an arena fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inwardly' keeps AT, the middle of hate.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the sword-fighters of Roman arenas, the ancient combatants.

clue.text: Numbers presented with hospital food

explanation.surface: Diners counted off and handed hospital food.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: Wiener's place of origin? Person in denial has skinned ferret for the heart

indicators.note: for the heart says the new letters replace the central letter of the ostrich word

parts.note: an ostrich is someone who buries their head in the sand

indicators.note: skinned means the outer letters of ferret are removed

explanation.surface: A hot dog's ancestry traced, with an ostrich and a skinned ferret thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinned' turns FERRET into ERRE, which replaces R, the central letter of OSTRICH. A Wiener is a Viennese person, not just a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Viennese person comes from Austria, whose German name this is.
